SOURCE EXCERPT:
Authorship on publications arising from university research follows the contribution standard set out below. A person qualifies as an author when they have made a substantial contribution to the design, acquisition, analysis, or interpretation of the work, and have approved the final manuscript. Acquisition of funding alone does not qualify a person for authorship, and neither does supervision of the laboratory in which the work was performed. Author order is determined by the contributing authors together, and this policy sets no default: the last position carries no special standing, and departments may not impose a convention that assigns it to the senior investigator. Disputes are mediated by the department chair and, failing that, by the Vice Provost for Research, whose determination is final and is recorded in writing to all authors.
